title: Monsoon and Rivergate
premise: Lena Almeida, a desert ranger who has spent years outrunning her past, is hired by her old rival Sef Marrow to escort a stolen ledger down the Rivergate before monsoon season seals the waterways. The ledger proves to be her dead father's inheritance—a map of debts and secrets that powerful families will kill to bury. Betrayed mid-river by Sef, Lena must survive the flood with a leaking boat, a found-family crew she never meant to love, and a stranger named Ivo who knows more about her father than she does. In the end, Lena chooses to stop running: she delivers the ledger not to a buyer but to the river towns it was written for, burning her claim to the inheritance and finding that family, not power, is what lasts.
about_author: Petra Vasquez is a former river guide who spent six seasons navigating monsoon waterways in Southeast Asia before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people who keep moving until they learn why they should stay.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Wasn't Running
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Tracking a thief across the salt flats, Lena catches him in hours but takes three days to bring him back—because stopping costs more than moving. The thief, a starving boy, asks why she chases people who've already lost. Her crew teases her about the emptiness she carries. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: Sef Marrow's Offer
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Old rival Sef Marrow arrives with gold and an apology: one job, escorting a sealed ledger down the Rivergate before the monsoon closes the passes. It's the route her father died on—the job sworn off long ago. The crew votes yes; money is thin. Lena says no, then packs anyway. Emotional beat: dread wearing the mask of pragmatism.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Weighs
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A quiet stranger joins at the dock, paying passage with knowledge instead of coin. When Lena inspects the ledger, she finds her father's handwriting: debts owed by every noble house on the river, and her own name listed as heir. Ivo watches her realize it. Emotional beat: inheritance as a wound reopened.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: Crew POV (rotating vignettes). The Rivergate narrows; rain begins. The crew—engineer Toma, cook Brisa, the boy thief Pip—becomes a family around card games and shared watch shifts. Sef grows distant, sending coded signals upstream. Lena teaches Pip to read stars. Emotional beat: found family forming without permission.

chapters.title: The First Leak
chapters.summary: Toma's POV. Sabotage: someone has bored holes below the waterline. Toma patches them through the night while the river rises. Suspicion fractures the crew—Ivo is accused, defends himself with a scar matching wounds from the same raid that killed Lena's father. Emotional beat: trust tested under rising water.

chapters.title: Monsoon Lock
chapters.summary: Brisa's POV. The storm hits full force; the lock gates ahead are chained shut by order of House Veyra—one of the debtor families. Armed riders demand the ledger. Sef reveals he sold them the route weeks ago. The crew fights free of the mooring into open floodwater rather than surrender. Emotional beat: betrayal made flesh; loyalty chosen over survival odds.

chapters.title: The Drowned Channel
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Off the maps, the crew runs the drowned channel where Lena's father's boat went down. Ivo confesses: he was her father's partner, the only survivor, who has spent ten years protecting the ledger from both houses and buyers like Sef. Lena rages, then grieves. Emotional beat: anger giving way to shared mourning.

chapters.title: What Power Buys
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Wrecked on a sandbar, they find Sef waiting with House Veyra's soldiers—he offers Lena her inheritance, legitimacy, everything her name entitles her to, if she hands over the ledger. She sees how power has hollowed him. Pip stands beside her when she refuses. Emotional beat: temptation answered with identity.

chapters.title: The Last of the Flood
chapters.summary: Full-crew climax. They run the flooded gorge in the leaking boat, Sef pursuing. Toma rigs the hull to vent steam; Brisa steers; Ivo and Lena hold the ledger against the spray. At the falls, Sef's boat founders; Lena turns back and pulls him out, refusing to become what he is. Emotional beat: mercy as victory.

chapters.title: Where the River Ends
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The storm breaks. Instead of selling or keeping the ledger, Lena reads its debts aloud in the river towns and lets each town decide what to do with its own names. She burns her page. The crew stays together—not because they're paid, but because they choose to. Emotional beat: stillness finally costing less than running.
